name: vs-code-ai-helper
description: AI-assisted task planning and implementation workflow for VS Code. Uses your existing AI subscriptions (Copilot, Claude, Codex, Gemini, Antigravity, Kiro) — real usage costs apply. AI runs can modify workspace files. Provided as-is with no warranty. See README and DISCLAIMER.md.

commands.title: Open Ensemble and Start New Task [Ctrl+Shift+O]

viewsWelcome.contents:
Configure a model before starting — Ensemble needs at least one AI model to run a task.
[Configure AI Models](command:vs-code-ai-helper.openAiModels)

Open a workspace folder to start tracking tasks. Ensemble stores task metadata in `.ensemble`.
[Start New Task](command:vs-code-ai-helper.startNewTask)

No tasks yet. Start one to see its workflow progress here.
[Start New Task](command:vs-code-ai-helper.startNewTask)

view/item/context.when: view == vs-code-ai-helper.tasksView && (viewItem == 'ensemble.task.creationRecovery.v1Recoverable' || viewItem == 'ensemble.task.creationRecovery.reconstructible' || viewItem == 'ensemble.task.creationRecovery.pristine' || viewItem == 'ensemble.task.creationRecovery.preservable' || viewItem == 'ensemble.task.creationRecovery.inspectionOnly')

ensemble.aiModelDefaults.description: Default AI models for Ensemble workflow stages.

ensemble.modelSettings.description: AI model and fallback settings for Ensemble workflow stages. Each stage entry may set primary, backups (ordered), strategy, and the optional skip flags primaryEnabled and backupsEnabled (the latter index-aligned with backups): a false flag skips that row during resolution while keeping its configured model and position; absent means enabled. A stage with no enabled model of its own falls back to the general (Task Description) model.

ensemble.showProviderAccountActions.description: Show the per-provider account-action buttons (Sign in / Switch account, Check usage) in the AI Models view's Provider Selection section. Hidden by default.

ensemble.warnings.unsavedSettings.description: Warn before discarding unsaved AI model settings.

ensemble.warnings.largeTokenRequest.description: Warn before a large AI token request.

ensemble.providerAccountLabels.description: Optional account/credential label per provider (e.g. "claude-cli": "work"), for users authenticated to the same CLI provider with more than one credential. No CLI provider reports which credential answered a run, so this is a manual declaration: it keys quota/entitlement tracking and paused-task state so two credentials sharing one provider stop being treated as the same account. Leave unset if you only use one credential per provider.

ensemble.fastForwardMaxIterations.description: Maximum rounds for one Fast Forward run (1–99, default 5). Applies only after a fast-forward is explicitly started — this cap never starts one by itself.

ensemble.autoAdvanceEnabled.description: Automatically advance the stage when a review meets the configured score. Off by default: a review runs exactly one round and stops. "auto-fast-forward" additionally runs Fast Forward Fixes when the destination is a review stage. Checked again immediately before each automatic dispatch, so turning it off also drops already-queued follow-ups.

ensemble.completeAndMoveOnTriggersAI.description: Start the destination stage's AI action after you click Complete Stage & Move On. Default "auto": exactly one AI action per click, never escalating to Fast Forward. "auto-fast-forward" opts in to continuing with the unattended review-and-fix loop. "off" starts nothing automatically.

ensemble.fastForwardUseAcceptanceThresho.description: Use the review acceptance threshold for Fast Forward.

ensemble.autoReviewAfterPlan.description: Start a high-level review automatically after AI drafts a plan. Off by default — unattended iteration is opt-in. "auto-fast-forward" continues with Fast Forward Fixes until the configured stop level.

ensemble.autoReviewAfterImplementation.description: Start a high-level review automatically after AI completes an implementation run. Off by default — unattended iteration is opt-in. "auto-fast-forward" continues with Fast Forward Fixes until the configured stop level.

enumDescriptions: Start implementation after Auto Advance accepts a plan review.
ensemble.autoImplementAfterReview.markdownDescription: Start implementation after **Auto Advance** moves an accepted plan review to Implementation. **⚠️ Warning: this makes real code and file changes automatically. Do not use without continuous human supervision.**

ensemble.allowDirtyWorktreeChanges.description: Allow AI changes with unrelated uncommitted workspace changes.

ensemble.desktopNotifications.description: Show native notifications for Ensemble attention requests.

match.description: Substring matched against a failed check's command line.

failureSignature.description: Substring matched against that failed check's output.

reason.description: Shown next to the quarantined failure so it stays explainable.

ensemble.knownFlakyChecks.markdownDescription: Completion checks whose failure is a known, pre-existing environmental issue rather than a real regression. A failure is only quarantined when both `match` and `failureSignature` are found — the raw pass/fail result is never altered, only the modulo-known-flakes signal shown to reviewers.

ensemble.reviewPlateauRounds.description: Consecutive review rounds with no new best score before a stage is considered plateaued and escalated for a human decision.

ensemble.completionCheckTimeoutMs.description: Maximum time (milliseconds) a single completion check (lint/type-check/test/explicit verification command) may run before being terminated, both at Publish and during every review round's verified-checks evidence collection.

ensemble.resilience.fastForwardSurvivesE.description: A plateau escalation raised inside a Fast Forward run no longer aborts that run: the run finishes its attempt budget and the escalation is reported at the end. Pauses from other sources (manual pause, another window) still abort. Turn off to restore the legacy behavior, where any pause aborts the run after one attempt.

ensemble.resilience.rejectDegenerateRevi.description: A review round with no parseable "Readiness: N/10" line is recorded as a failed attempt (with a reason in the run log) instead of being appended to the review score history — so a failed provider call can never wear a 0/10 score and manufacture a false plateau. Turn off to restore the legacy behavior.

ensemble.resilience.zeroFixableTerminate.description: Two consecutive review rounds that each carry positive evidence of zero task-fixable blockers (a parsed empty blocker block or an explicit no-blockers statement) end Fast Forward as success, regardless of score movement. The score-improvement gate remains an additional way to succeed, and neither path ends the run while a plan-progress marker still reports steps outstanding. Turn off to restore the legacy behavior, where only a score gain can end the loop successfully.

ensemble.resilience.blockerSetPlateau.description: Stall detection compares the reported blocker set across rounds (matched on category, resolver, and the file/subject named — not exact wording) instead of the review score's high-water mark: a shrinking or changing set counts as progress regardless of score; an unchanged or growing set escalates. Turn off to restore legacy score-based plateau detection.

ensemble.resilience.churnCeilingRounds.description: Escalate unconditionally after this many consecutive review rounds without a decrease in task-fixable blockers, independent of score movement and blocker churn. 0 disables the ceiling (legacy behavior). Keep it well below ensemble.fastForwardMaxIterations so a churning loop stops before it burns its full budget.

ensemble.resilience.nothingToFixRoutesTo.description: An implementation round that reports completion without changing any files — when prior rounds already changed the tree — routes onward to review instead of being recorded as a failed run. A correct implementer that finds the plan already satisfied is not forced to fabricate work. Turn off to restore the legacy behavior, where zero changed files is a hard failure.

ensemble.resilience.noProgressBreakerRou.description: Stop and escalate after this many consecutive implementation rounds that change zero files while the same blocker persists, instead of iterating to ensemble.fastForwardMaxIterations. 0 disables the breaker (legacy behavior). Works together with ensemble.resilience.nothingToFixRoutesToReview, which is what lets zero-change rounds continue at all.

ensemble.resilience.quotaResetNearThresh.description: When a quota/rate-limit or model-entitlement failure carries a provider-reported reset time within this many hours, remedy messages say to rerun after that local time; beyond it, messages advise switching the stage's model instead of waiting. When no reset time is known at all, messages keep offering both options (rerun or switch), unchanged from before this setting existed.

ensemble.resilience.inactivityTimeoutMin.description: Kill a CLI run's process tree when it has produced no stdout/stderr/raw-transport output for this many consecutive minutes, distinct from the flat 60-minute wall-clock cap on a run. OFF BY DEFAULT (0): output silence is a poor proxy for a wedged process — an agentic CLI reading and editing a large file legitimately goes quiet for long stretches, and killing it destroys that round's work. The wall clock already bounds the worst case. Enable it (45 is a reasonable starting point) only if you actually see runs hang; a value near 60 is equivalent to the wall clock and does nothing.

vs-code-ai-helper.aiModelDefaults.markdownDescription: Legacy per-stage AI model IDs, superseded by `#ensemble.modelSettings#`. Bare IDs are GitHub Copilot models; prefixed IDs (e.g. `claude-cli:sonnet`, `codex-cli:default`, `gemini-cli:gemini-2.5-pro`, `antigravity-cli:default`, `kiro-cli:default`) run through the vendor's subscription CLI. Configure via **Ensemble: Configure AI Models per Step**.

vs-code-ai-helper.modelSettings.description: Primary and backup models per stage, along with fallback strategy. Configure via Ensemble Settings.

vs-code-ai-helper.warnings.unsavedSettin.description: Warn before discarding unsaved changes in the AI Models panel. The warning dialog offers "Don't show again", which sets this to false.

vs-code-ai-helper.warnings.largeTokenReq.description: Warn before sending a large AI prompt that may use significant quota. The warning dialog offers "Proceed and don't ask again", which sets this to false.

vs-code-ai-helper.enabledProviders.description: Provider Selection. Providers are disabled until explicitly enabled.

vs-code-ai-helper.fastForwardMaxIteratio.description: Maximum rounds for one Fast Forward run (1–99, default 5). Applies only after a fast-forward is explicitly started — this cap never starts one by itself. Ignored whenever any ensemble.fastForwardMaxIterations value is set.

enumDescriptions: Automatically advance when the configured review score threshold is reached.
Auto-advance and run Fast Forward Fixes where applicable (when the destination is a review stage).
vs-code-ai-helper.autoAdvanceEnabled.description: Auto-advance when the configured review score threshold is reached. Off by default: a review runs exactly one round and stops. Legacy true/false values are still honored (true = auto). Ignored whenever any ensemble.autoAdvanceEnabled value is set.

enumDescriptions: Do not start the destination stage's AI action.
Automatically start the AI action for the destination stage.
Start the AI action and continue with Fast Forward Fixes once it reaches a review (directly for Publish, after plan generation or implementation for the other stages).
vs-code-ai-helper.completeAndMoveOnTrigg.description: When completing a stage and moving on, automatically start the AI action for the destination stage. Default "auto": exactly one AI action per click, never escalating to Fast Forward. Legacy true/false values are still honored (true = auto). Ignored whenever any ensemble.completeAndMoveOnTriggersAI value is set.

vs-code-ai-helper.autoAdvanceScoreThresh.description: Score required for auto-advance (1–10). Lower thresholds intentionally permit earlier advancement; the extension does not impose a universal minimum acceptable score.

vs-code-ai-helper.fastForwardStopLevel.description: Fast-forward target score. 0 stops after any improvement; 1–10 continues until that score.

vs-code-ai-helper.fastForwardUseAcceptan.description: Use the review acceptance threshold instead of the fast-forward stop level.

enumDescriptions: Start high-level review after AI drafts a plan.
Start the review and run Fast Forward Fixes until the configured stop level.
vs-code-ai-helper.autoReviewAfterPlan.description: Start high-level review after AI drafts a plan. Off by default — unattended iteration is opt-in. Legacy true/false values are still honored (true = auto). Ignored whenever any ensemble.autoReviewAfterPlan value is set.

enumDescriptions: Start high-level review after AI completes initial implementation.
Start the review and run Fast Forward Fixes until the configured stop level.
vs-code-ai-helper.autoReviewAfterImpleme.description: Start high-level review after AI completes initial implementation. Off by default — unattended iteration is opt-in. Legacy true/false values are still honored (true = auto). Ignored whenever any ensemble.autoReviewAfterImplementation value is set.

vs-code-ai-helper.allowDirtyWorktreeChan.description: Automatically proceed with AI implementation/Fast Forward runs even when the workspace has unrelated uncommitted changes, without prompting first.

vs-code-ai-helper.desktopNotifications.description: Show a native OS notification when Ensemble is waiting on you to answer a question or a run fails outright. Off by default.

vs-code-ai-helper.publishVerificationCom.description: Explicit verification command lines the Publish stage runs (in the task's Publish verification scope) instead of auto-detecting package.json lint/test scripts. Leave empty to use script auto-detection.

scripts.compile: pnpm run check-types && pnpm run lint && node esbuild.js
scripts.package: pnpm run check-types && pnpm run lint && node esbuild.js --production && pnpm run verify:workflow-safety
scripts.verify:vscode-1.93-compat: pnpm run check-types:vscode-1.93-compat && node scripts/runWorkflowSuite.mjs vscode-lm-compat
